references.text: The Israelites willingly gave gold and earrings to make the golden calf, in a similar way to how they here gave gold rings to Gideon
The Israelites gave voluntary offerings of gold and jewelry for the tabernacle, showing the people's willingness to give valuable items
War spoils of gold jewelry and earrings were given as an offering to the Lord after victory in battle, like Gideon's collection of spoils
The preceding verse explains that the Midianites had gold rings because they were Ishmaelites, which provides context for the gift
The following verses describe what Gideon did with the gold rings—he made an ephod that became a snare for Israel
Gold rings (nezem) are mentioned as valuable gifts and jewelry in the time of the patriarchs
